what_worked: Lorenz curve with Gini, anonymity paradox, and selection-bias diagram form a genuinely original analytical arc.
fix_next: Disclose missing-value rates for category (27%) and audience_type (29%) before making claims that depend on those fields.
verdict: Exceptional storytelling with a few unchecked numbers; disclose missingness to earn full trust.
factual_error_detail: Slide 5: AI median MRR stated as $446 vs reference $503 (material). Slide 4: anonymous count 130 vs reference 129 (minor). Slide 3: 22% zero-revenue vs 216/1000=21.6% (minor rounding). Slide 5: B2B/B2C '$49/$9 revenue per customer' doesn't map to any reference metric (unverifiable, possibly conflating ARPU with median multiples).

evidence.insight: Slide 3 Gini 0.906 and Lorenz framing, slide 4 anonymous-cohort median $9,008 vs $253, slide 6 dual selection-bias argument, slide 7 zero-revenue listings for sale — each is decision-useful and non-obvious.
evidence.narrative: Clean arc from headline optimism (slide 2) through inequality (3), anonymity paradox (4), signal testing (5), epistemological caveat (6), market pricing (7), to a memorable landing (8). Every slide advances one claim; no filler.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets scope and freeze date; slide 6 explicitly addresses survivorship and selection bias. However, ~27% missing category and ~29% missing audience_type are never disclosed, weakening slides 5's category and B2B/B2C claims.
evidence.accuracy: Top-10 share 'half' ≈ 49.6% is fine. $15.6M monthly total matches reference. AI median $446 vs $503 is a real miss. 130 vs 129 anonymous is minor. 22% vs 21.6% zero-revenue is acceptable rounding. B2B/B2C per-customer figures are not traceable to reference metrics.
evidence.visual: Two-color palette (gold, charcoal) used with discipline throughout. Lorenz curve annotated at three points. Slide 4 proportional bar is effective. Slide 6 dark-background selection-bias diagram is a strong conceptual visualization. Typography hierarchy is consistent and elegant. No chart junk.

change_reason: Lowered framing from 8.5 to 8.0: the presentation never discloses substantial missingness in category and audience_type fields, which directly underpin claims on slides 5 and 7. All other scores confirmed.
